T1_target_vs_control.interpretation: the layer is ANTI-SELECTIVE: negative-control modules carry larger standardised effects than analgesic-target modules (median |z| 2.47 vs 1.07, two-sided MWU p=0.0019). This is stronger than 'no discrimination'

T2_randset_null_selectivity.interpretation: control modules are over-represented among randset-significant tests (14/32 vs base rate 30/132, binomial p=0.0067): the null that 'confirms' targets also confirms controls

T4_target_rank_percentile.interpretation: analgesic targets sit just below the median of the effect-size distribution (target median |z| 1.0729 = 44.7th percentile; no enrichment)

T3_single_cell_power.interpretation: gene-level DE is well powered (detected Ifit2 at logFC -0.048, q=0.042); the ~55% drop in myeloid fraction is underpowered (observed d=1.267 vs MDE d=2.38) and is an inconclusive null, not evidence of equality

T5_reversal_score_power.design: KO/OE exact mirrors, r=-1.000; each Delta is one estimate (no independent 2v2 arm); SE = bootstrap SE of Delta
T5_reversal_score_power.interpretation: the layer has per-test signal (MDE = 2.8 x median SE 0.0185 = 0.0518 log-units, normal approx; 0.1046 t-based; largest target Delta 0.274 = 5.3 x MDE; 31/132 tests exact p<0.05), but it resolves large effects only: the median target |Delta| 0.031 lies below MDE, and only 41/102 targets exceed it. The failure is anti-selectivity (see T1/T2) plus a power floor for the median target, not a total absence of signal
